newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PNG/Bougainville peace talks formally open in NZ.
newsitem.headline: PNG/Bougainville peace talks formally open in NZ.

text.p: Talks aimed at ending nine years of secessionist fighting on Papua New Guinea's Bougainville Island formally opened in New Zealand on Saturday.
New Zealand Foreign Minister Don McKinnon, who welcomed the meeting's 50 participants, said he hoped for progress in the preliminary discussions which will involve Bougainville parties only.

Representives of the three main groups, the PNG-backed Bougainville Transitional Government, the Bougainville Interim Government and its associate the Bougainville Revolutionary Army, were flown into New Zealand early on Saturday.
Ministry officials said talks were set to get underway later in the afternoon.

"There were many logistical dificulties involved in bringing your groups together and inevitably some people have not been able to come," McKinnon said in an welcoming address at Burnham Military Camp near the South Island city of Christchurch.
"We hope you find this neutral environment...conducive to discussing your issues."
Thousands have died in fighting on the resource-rich island which lies to the southeast of the main Papua New Guinea archipelago and neighbours the Solomon Islands.
Previous attempts at internationally-brokered peace talks since the early 1990s have failed to produce concrete results.
"History tells us there is no easy way through this process, but that is no reason for you not to try and lay a solid foundation here at Burnham for future discussions," the minister added.
